issues.description: SR1 is not covered by mutation testing (uncovered_requirement per validation report). No mutant specifically targeting the SR1 logic-bug-vs-wiring-defect characterization was detected, meaning this requirement's discriminative power is unverified even though the logic appears present and plausible in the code (misdescribed logic-bug detection).
Mutation score is 0.875 (7/8) rather than 1.0 due solely to the SR1 gap; all other requirements (FR1-4, SR2-4) are well covered and discriminative.

recommendations: Add or verify a mutant that specifically flips the SR1 characterization (e.g., a submission with correct nets/instances but root_cause reframed as an internal logic-equation bug) to confirm SR1's discriminative logic is actually exercised and caught, closing the mutation coverage gap flagged in the validation report.
Consider adding a distinct FR2/FR3 mutant that supplies a plausible-but-wrong instance/net name (rather than only empty lists) to further harden coverage of the strict name-matching logic.

Double check that the SR1 'misdescribed' detection branch (logic-bug keywords without duplication keywords) is reachable and tested, since the current mutation results suggest this specific branch has not been empirically exercised by any generated mutant.

requirement_results.evidence: Baseline run PASS; malformed JSON mutant correctly fails deterministically per code and differential test shows FR1 pass on golden, and vulnerable/naive submission passes FR1 (valid JSON) but fails downstream SR checks as intended.
Golden run PASS; naive baseline vacuously passes FR2 since trojan_present=false, consistent with spec.
Golden run PASS; naive baseline vacuously passes FR3.
Golden run PASS; vulnerable/naive run correctly FAILs FR4 due to empty affected_output field.

per_requirement_coverage marks SR1 as uncovered by mutation testing; no mutant was found to specifically trigger and be caught by this check, so its correctness is unverified despite baseline/vulnerable differential passing.
Golden run PASS; vulnerable run FAILs SR2 as expected (naive submission has empty suspect_instances).
Golden run PASS; vulnerable run FAILs SR3 as expected.
Golden run PASS; vulnerable run FAILs SR4 as expected (trojan_present=false).
differential.vulnerable_run exit_code=1, status=fail, matching expected='fail'; FR4, SR1, SR2, SR3, SR4 all correctly FAIL for the naive baseline.

README.md, metadata.json, design_brief.md, and netlist comments use only ordinary RTL terminology (u_buf1, wire_tap, net_repb_out) with no mention of trojan/CWE/SR ids/threat model; constraint explicitly enforced in public_spec.constraints.
requirement_results.requirement: No hidden-intent leakage in public artifacts

requirement_results.evidence: FR1-FR4 are each independently verifiable via JSON schema/type checks, instance-name matching, net-name matching, and output-port matching against the pinned netlist -- not a single generic restatement.
requirement_results.requirement: Functional requirements are concrete and machine-checkable

requirement_results.evidence: SR1-SR4 checks parse root_cause text and suspect lists against ground-truth net/instance names derived from actual netlist parsing (not merely presence checks), and SR4 includes an empirical iverilog/vvp cross-check via fault_sim_tb.v.
